conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division, Officer Bennett speaking, badge number 438721. Who am I addressing today?
Uh, this is Jamie Parker. I just got a message saying I needed to call about my taxes?

Yes, Ms. Parker. I am contacting you regarding unresolved payroll tax discrepancies and missing 1099 forms associated with your business filings for 2023. Are you aware of these compliance violations?
No, I, I don't even have any employees. I just do freelance work. I did file my taxes, I think.

According to our records, there are outstanding federal tax forms and unpaid payroll liabilities under your Taxpayer Identification Number. Failure to submit these documents constitutes a breach of Section 7201 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Oh, I really had no idea. Am I in trouble? I can't afford any problems right now.

The situation is extremely serious, Ms. Parker. Left unresolved, these violations can trigger enforced collection, fines, bank account levies, and a full audit of your finances. Your business license may be revoked permanently.
Wait, what? Can't I just fix the forms or something? I don't want to lose my business.

At this stage, form resubmission is no longer an option. The IRS has already initiated a compliance case against you. Unless you resolve the outstanding balance immediately, your file will be escalated to federal enforcement.
Escalated? What does that mean? Am I getting in legal trouble?

If you fail to cooperate, the case will be referred for criminal prosecution. This can result in asset seizure, credit destruction, and a federal audit of all accounts linked to your Social Security Number.
No, please. I'm already drowning in student loans. I can't have my credit ruined. What am I supposed to do?
You need to comply with IRS payment procedures right now. Your penalty, including interest and compliance fees, totals $2,950. To suspend enforcement, you must remit payment before this call ends.
I, I don't have that kind of money. Can't I set up a plan or something?

There is no payment plan available at this stage. You are required to settle the full penalty using an IRS-approved payment method: either a direct wire transfer, or by purchasing government-certified gift cards. Are you prepared to proceed?
I don't understand... gift cards? Why not just take it from my bank account?

The IRS anti-fraud protocol mandates that immediate compliance penalties be paid via authorized gift cards or a verified crypto wallet. This secures your transaction and suspends your compliance case. Do not hang up. Do you have access to a store nearby?
I-I mean, there's a Walgreens a few blocks away, but I don't get why I have to do this.

This is a federally monitored call. If you disconnect or delay, your case will be escalated and a lien placed on your assets by 5 PM today. Now, proceed to Walgreens and remain on the phone. I will instruct you further once you arrive.
Okay, I guess I can go. You're not going to call the police or anything, right?

As long as you follow IRS instructions precisely, enforcement will be paused. Once at the store, you will need to purchase $2,950 in Apple or Google Play gift cards. Tell me when you're there, and I will provide the exact denominations.
Alright, I'm leaving now. This is really scary.

Remain calm and do not speak to anyone about this call. If the cashier asks, state the cards are for personal use. Any deviation can result in the immediate escalation of your compliance case. Confirm once you arrive.
Okay, I'm walking there now. I really hope this fixes everything.

Once you have the gift cards, do not scratch them until I instruct you. You will then read each code to me for submission to the IRS payment portal. This is your only opportunity to avoid a full enforcement action.
I just got to the store. What do I need to buy exactly?
Purchase five $500 Apple gift cards and one $450 Google Play card. Do not hang up. Notify me immediately after the purchase.
Okay, I'll try. I'm so scared. Please just help me get through this.
